title: Print invoice due dates with chrono
summary: Slicing strings gives a due date of 09/53/2026. Fix it with NaiveDate and format, then read offset timestamps as DateTime<Utc>.

turns.user: invoice due dates show stuff like 09/53/2026 lol. chrono is already in Cargo.toml, use it. format should look like Oct 23, 2026

assistant.body: Sure! The code slices the day out of the string and adds 30, so any month boundary gives you a 53rd. NaiveDate::parse_from_str reads it as a real date, Days::new(30) moves it forward, and format writes it back out. %-d is the day without zero padding. An impossible date like February 30 now comes back as a ParseError instead of a panic, so the caller can deal with it. For a date with no time of day, NaiveDate is the best practice.

turns.user: oh wait the API changed, field is issued_at now and it sends 2026-09-23T15:30:00+09:00 style. due date should be UTC

assistant.body: Now that the value carries a time and an offset, NaiveDate cannot read it. parse_from_str rejects the leftover T15:30:00+09:00 as trailing input. DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339 reads it, with_timezone(&Utc) turns it into a DateTime<Utc>, and date_naive takes the date part. Note: an invoice issued before 9 in the morning Japan time falls on the previous day in UTC, so its due date moves one day earlier too.
